I've been working this land for 40 years. I know Quzhou's soil, I know the weather, I know what works. My back isn't what it was at 40, but my wife and I can still manage 15 mu between us if I plan it right.

Most of my land — about 10 mu — stays in the wheat-maize rotation. That's what my father did, that's what everyone around here does, and it works. I plant wheat in October when the ground cools, then after harvest in June I go straight into maize on the same fields. For wheat I'll use the improved variety I've been buying from the county seed station for years. For maize I use hybrid seed — the yields are just better, even I can see that. My well gives me control others don't have, so I'm not worried about dry spells.

The other 5 mu I keep in cotton. Cotton is harder work and my joints feel it, but the price is still good and I know how to grow it. I'll plough those fields in spring before transplanting. Cotton needs more water and more spraying than anything else I grow — bollworm pressure here means I cannot skip applications, or I'll lose the whole crop.

I use fertilizer the way I always have — heavy enough to get a good yield, not so much that I waste money. For wheat and maize I rotary till or go no-till after wheat to save time. At 63 with two people, every hour of labor counts.
